headline: ASX surges 1.6% to close at 8,732 as CBA hits a fresh high, while MSFT jumped 5.5% last night on strong momentum — but GOOGL slipped 2.5%.

portfolio.summary: A mixed bag across the portfolio today. CBA was the standout on the ASX, closing up 2.2% to $165.02 — a strong session for the bank. FUEL.AX slipped 1.6% as oil prices fell last night. On the US side (last night's session), MSFT had a cracker — up 5.5% to $450.24 — while GOOGL shed 2.5% to $380.34. TTWO nudged up 2.9%. The Vanguard ETFs were all quietly positive.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Big night for Microsoft last session — up 5.5% to USD $450.24. Strong momentum, likely driven by continued enthusiasm around its AI products and cloud growth. Compare that to Amazon, whose revenue trends have been drawing less favourable comparisons lately.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google gave back 2.5% last session, closing at USD $380.34. No specific news today, but the stock has been under pressure as Microsoft and others gain ground in the AI race.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two closed up 2.9% last session at USD $224.16. Rockstar Games (a Take-Two studio) made headlines with GTA 6 developers announcing a union — a major first for the gaming industry.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank
movers.note: CBA had a strong session today, closing up 2.2% at $165.02. The broader ASX financials sector benefited from a solid market day, with the ASX 200 up 1.6%.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 1.6% today to $8.46, tracking a fall in oil prices last night (WTI crude down 1.7% to $87.36). Goldman Sachs is also warning that energy markets may be entering a 'demand destruction phase' — meaning high prices are starting to cause people and businesses to use less energy, which pushes prices down.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Quiet positive session for VDHG, up 0.8% to $76.00 on the back of a strong ASX day.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid session today, closing up 1.6% at 8,732 — a meaningful one-day gain. Last night in the US, both the S&P 500 (+0.2% to 7,580) and NASDAQ (+0.2% to 26,973) nudged up modestly. Gold surged 2.1% to a lofty USD $4,593/oz, suggesting investors are still seeking safe havens. Oil fell 1.7% to $87.36. The Aussie dollar is sitting at USD 71.86 cents, up slightly.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong close today — up 1.6% for the session.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — modest gains of 0.2%.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's session — flat to slightly positive.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell 1.7% last night — headwind for FUEL.AX.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold surged 2.1% last night — investors still keen on safe havens.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar up slightly at ~71.9 US cents.

politics.summary: A busy weekend for Australian economic policy. The RBA has lifted the cash rate (the interest rate it sets for banks, which flows through to mortgages and savings accounts), and Albanese's government is looking to the Greens to push through a tax plan that hit some turbulence after the election. GDP data is also due this week — a key read on how the economy is tracking.

stories.title: Savings account rates rise after RBA cash rate hike
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA has raised its cash rate again, meaning banks are now passing higher interest rates on to savings accounts. If you've got a high-interest savings account, you may see your rate nudge up — that's the silver lining. The flip side is that anyone with a variable-rate mortgage will be paying more. Worth checking your bank's current rate.

stories.title: GDP data tops the agenda this week, RBA officials to speak
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's GDP (Gross Domestic Product — the total value of everything the economy produces) figures are due this week, and RBA officials are scheduled to speak publicly. These numbers will give the clearest picture yet of whether the economy is slowing down as rate hikes bite. Markets will be watching closely for any hint about what the RBA does next with interest rates.

stories.title: Albanese banks on Greens to pass tax plan after election backflip
stories.why_it_matters: After shifting its position on tax policy post-election, the Albanese government is now leaning on the Greens in the Senate to get its tax legislation through. The details of the specific tax plan aren't fully outlined in the article, but it signals the government will need to negotiate and potentially make concessions to minor parties. This could affect tax settings relevant to investors and property owners depending on what's ultimately agreed.

ai.summary: This week's AI conversation has swung between big-picture governance debates and practical tools. The Vatican and Pope Leo XIV have been vocal on AI ethics — calling for a ban on lethal autonomous weapons and warning about AI monopolies. Meanwhile, a useful concept called 'meta-cognitive regulation' is getting attention as the key skill for working effectively with AI tools.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV calls on EU to ban lethal autonomous AI weapons
stories.why_it_matters: Pope Leo XIV has publicly backed the EU's push to ban AI-powered weapons that can kill without a human deciding to pull the trigger — so-called 'lethal autonomous weapons'. The Pope's argument is that machines should never make life-or-death decisions. It's a rare case of the Catholic Church wading into tech regulation, and it adds moral pressure on European policymakers who are already debating AI weapons rules. Not an immediate market mover, but it shapes the regulatory environment for defence-tech companies.

stories.title: Vatican's 'AI Monopolies' talk risks encouraging bad tech policy — ITIF pushes back
stories.why_it_matters: The Vatican has been warning about big tech companies having too much control over AI — what they call 'AI monopolies'. A leading US tech policy think tank (ITIF) is pushing back, arguing this framing could lead to heavy-handed regulations that actually slow down innovation without solving real problems. The debate matters because it feeds directly into how governments — including the EU — decide to regulate companies like Google (GOOGL) and Microsoft (MSFT).

stories.title: Meta-cognitive regulation: the AI skill nobody's talking about
stories.why_it_matters: A growing argument in AI circles is that the most valuable skill isn't knowing how to use specific tools, but 'meta-cognitive regulation' — basically, understanding your own thinking process well enough to guide an AI effectively. In plain terms: knowing when to trust AI output, when to push back, and how to break down problems so the AI can actually help. As AI tools become standard in workplaces, this kind of self-awareness about how you think and problem-solve may matter more than technical know-how.

sport.summary: A big weekend of NRL with some upsets and a heartbreaking off-field story dominating the headlines. The Dragons snapped their losing streak with a stunning upset of the Broncos in Brisbane, while the Raiders are currently thumping the Cowboys. And Ben Cousins' MND diagnosis has shaken the whole sporting community.

stories.title: Ben Cousins diagnosed with MND — AFL world in shock
stories.why_it_matters: AFL legend Ben Cousins has been diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease (MND) — a progressive disease that attacks the nervous system and has no cure. The news has devastated the AFL community, with players, coaches and fans rallying around the Cousins family. Cousins, one of the most celebrated but also troubled figures in Australian football, had spoken publicly about trying to rebuild his life in recent years. This is a genuinely heartbreaking story.

stories.title: Dragons end losing streak with stunning upset of the Broncos
stories.why_it_matters: The St George Illawarra Dragons pulled off arguably the upset of the season, beating the Brisbane Broncos 30-26 at Suncorp Stadium today. The Dragons had been on a horror losing run and were massive underdogs heading into the game. The win will be a massive confidence boost for the red-and-white, while the Broncos will be licking their wounds at home.

stories.title: Raiders pummel Cowboys in Canberra — live in 2nd half
stories.why_it_matters: The Raiders are currently leading the Cowboys 26-12 in the second half at GIO Stadium in Canberra. The Raiders have been in dominant form today, turning on the style in front of the home crowd. Result still to be confirmed — check the app for the final score.

stories.title: Wests Tigers edge Bulldogs in controversial match
stories.why_it_matters: Wests Tigers beat the Bulldogs 22-16 at CommBank Stadium on Saturday, but the result was overshadowed by a string of controversial refereeing calls. The Bulldogs were furious post-match, with the ABC reporting the Tigers 'dodged a bullet'. The refs are under the microscope again — expect plenty of noise from the Bulldogs camp this week.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Big jump last night — riding the AI wave
watch_today.detail: Microsoft surged 5.5% last session to USD $450.24. That's a strong move — likely driven by ongoing enthusiasm for its AI products (Copilot, Azure AI) and comparisons that put it ahead of Amazon on revenue trends. No reason to sell into strength here; the momentum is real. Hold and let it run.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Slipping while competitors surge
watch_today.detail: Google dropped 2.5% last session to $380.34, and the narrative continues to favour Microsoft and others in the AI space. No company-specific bad news today, but the relative underperformance is worth watching. No need to panic, but keep an eye on whether this gap keeps widening when Google reports next.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Goldman warns of 'demand destruction' in energy markets
watch_today.detail: FUEL fell 1.6% today as oil slid 1.7% last night to $87.36. Goldman Sachs is now warning that energy markets may be entering a 'demand destruction phase' — meaning prices are high enough that consumers and businesses are cutting back, which pushes prices lower. This is a headwind for FUEL.AX over the coming weeks. Worth watching, but no need to bail just yet.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Rockstar Games workers form a union — watch for cost implications
watch_today.detail: GTA 6 developers at Rockstar Games (owned by Take-Two) have announced a union — a first for a major AAA game studio. Unions typically lead to better pay and conditions for workers, which is good news for the people making the game, but could mean higher development costs for Take-Two down the track. TTWO is up 2.9% despite the news, so the market isn't panicking. Hold, but keep this on the radar as negotiations develop.

watch_today.title: Australia GDP data due this week — could move the ASX
watch_today.detail: Australia's GDP figures drop this week, and they'll be a key signal on whether the RBA's rate hikes are slowing the economy as intended. If growth is weaker than expected, it could fuel hopes the RBA is done hiking — good for shares generally. If growth holds up, more rate hikes may be on the table. Keep an eye on this mid-week.
